subject.title: fix(ollama): remote Ollama streaming stalls at model_call:started on slow hosts

question: Should native Ollama streams treat models.providers.<id>.timeoutSeconds as an idle/no-progress timeout while chunks arrive, or preserve the documented total guarded-fetch cap?
rationale: The code change is narrow and matches sibling streaming wrappers, but it changes an existing documented timeout behavior that some users may rely on as a wall-clock cap.

options.title: Accept idle timeout after proof
options.body: Proceed if the contributor adds real remote/slow Ollama proof and docs are updated to say streamed chunks refresh the timeout.

options.title: Preserve total timeout contract
options.body: Ask for a different fix that keeps timeoutSeconds as a total wall-clock cap during body streaming.

options.title: Pause for live root-cause proof
options.body: Hold this PR until maintainers or the contributor reproduce the reported remote-host stall and confirm this callback is the root cause.

recommendation.title: Accept idle timeout after proof
recommendation.body: Proceed if the contributor adds real remote/slow Ollama proof and docs are updated to say streamed chunks refresh the timeout.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest recent history on the Ollama stream code that would own the timeout behavior choice.
